players.product: NVL72-class Rubin rack systems / GB-series servers

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 revenue of NT$2.53 trillion, up 41% YoY and 19% QoQ, a record for the quarter, beating the outlook given at the May call; cloud & networking products topped half of revenue for the first time. Gross margin 6.12% (down 0.21pp YoY on product mix) but gross profit up 36%; operating margin 3.75% (up 0.6pp); operating income NT$948 hundred million, up 68% YoY - the highest single quarter in company history. Net profit NT$600 hundred million (+35% YoY, +20% QoQ) and EPS NT$4.27 (+34%), both records for the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue NT$2.53 trillion +41% YoY / +19% QoQ; GM 6.12%; OPM 3.75%; operating income NT$948 hundred million +68% (record); net profit NT$600 hundred million +35%; EPS NT$4.27 +34%

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026: revenue NT$4.65 trillion +35% YoY, operating income NT$1705 hundred million +65%, net profit NT$1099 hundred million +27%, EPS NT$7.84 +26%; H1 operating margin 3.67% (+0.67pp) and ROE 6.21% versus a 12% full-year target. Adjusted EBITDA grew 52% YoY, up NT$776 hundred million. July revenue crossed the NT$9000 hundred-million single-month mark for the first time - a record set before the peak season even began, which management credits to AI server demand (an infrastructure business with little seasonality) smoothing out consumer-electronics cycles.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 revenue NT$4.65 trillion +35%; operating income NT$1705 hundred million +65%; net profit NT$1099 hundred million +27%; EPS NT$7.84; OPM 3.67%; ROE 6.21%; July first month ever above NT$9000 hundred million

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 guided to significant QoQ growth and strong YoY growth as AI keeps growing and ICT enters its seasonal peak; full-year outlook of strong growth is maintained with visibility better than in May. AI rack shipments are expected to grow high double digits QoQ in Q3 as the new platform launches, and full-year guidance of more-than-doubling AI rack shipments is unchanged. Full-year operating margin is expected to exceed last year's 3.2%, with a 3%+ level maintained mid/long term. Capital expenditure is guided to rise more than thirty percent this year (H1 capex NT$809 hundred million, +5% YoY) to pre-expand server, rack, liquid-cooling and testing capacity, including localized US capacity in Texas, Wisconsin, Ohio and California plus Taiwan, Mexico and Vietnam.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3: significant QoQ / strong YoY growth; Q3 AI rack shipments +high double digits QoQ; full-year AI rack shipments to more than double; FY operating margin above 3.2%; H1 capex NT$809 hundred million +5%

quarterly_data.signal: New-generation AI rack (Vera Rubin) on plan: volume production from Q3 (production preparation in Q3) with shipments starting in Q4, ramping over subsequent quarters to become the main product next year. Foxconn is still working toward roughly half of the new-platform market and argues product standardization raises rather than lowers entry barriers, favoring suppliers with scale delivery and vertical integration - its new-generation Compute Tray line reached 100% automation. Next year's overall rack volume hinges on how much CoWoS capacity the chip customers secure; the market expects CoWoS capacity to grow more than 50% next year, with final rack output depending on chip supply. GB-platform demand remains stable and GB-series demand should last at least into next year.
quarterly_data.figure: Rubin racks: volume production from Q3, shipments from Q4, main product next year; new-platform share target about half; market expects CoWoS capacity +50% next year; Compute Tray automation 100%

quarterly_data.signal: Order visibility is improving in step with rising CSP capex: Foxconn already clearly sees orders continuing upward next year. North American CSP capex is expected to approach US$800 billion this year and to cross the one-trillion-dollar threshold soon. AI compute demand comes from four buckets - LLM model builders, CSPs and neoclouds, governments, and enterprises - with model builders and CSP/neocloud the main sources today; contributions from new-type cloud (neocloud) customers should start showing before the end of this year, and sovereign AI and large-enterprise engagements are expanding.
quarterly_data.figure: order visibility extends into next year and is still rising; 2026 NA CSP capex approaching US$8000 hundred million

quarterly_data.signal: ASIC momentum: last year roughly one tenth of AI server revenue came from ASIC servers; in H1 2026 the ASIC revenue share was already slightly above last year's full-year level, with new customers and new projects added this year. Because ASIC projects mostly run on a consignment model, reported revenue understates the real business scale. Market estimates put ASIC at about 28% of AI-server shipments this year, rising toward about 40% by 2030; Foxconn targets a 40%-plus ASIC market share, offering both GPU and ASIC solutions and taking roles from modules and cooling systems to compute-tray and rack integration.
quarterly_data.figure: ASIC about 28% of AI server shipments in 2026 rising toward 40% by 2030 (market estimate); Foxconn ASIC share target above 40%; H1 2026 ASIC revenue share above last year's full-year level

quarterly_data.signal: Standalone racks beyond the GPU flagship - customer CPU racks, LPU racks and switch racks (including Vera CPU racks) - enter production in Q3 and ramp gradually in Q4, with larger-scale shipments next year. Their unit value is below GPU AI racks, so the revenue and gross-profit impact is comparatively limited, but they let Foxconn supply whatever platform a customer needs, mostly with zero-to-one design plus scale manufacturing.

GB-platform demand remains very stable, and GB-series product demand is expected to continue at least into next year even as the new-generation platform ramps; overall AI rack shipment growth expectations are unchanged.

Agentic AI is lifting general-purpose server demand on top of AI training and inference; the overall GP server market grows double digits this year, H2 up double digits versus H1, and visibility is better than three months ago. Industry estimates put 2026 general-purpose server CPU shipment growth at about 16%, rising to about 23% next year. As the leading global server ODM with long CSP and brand relationships, Foxconn expects its general-purpose and CPU-server business to outgrow the industry average.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 general-purpose server CPU shipments +16% (industry estimate), about +23% next year

quarterly_data.signal: Computing end products are expected to decline slightly QoQ in Q3 as the new-product demand peak passes and memory supply is tight; however, component price increases are lifting shipment prices, so YoY growth remains significant.

contracts.signal: Among recent major events, Foxconn and Intel are jointly promoting a next-generation AI platform.

players.product: AI server racks with integrated optical networking

quarterly_data.signal: H1 networking-product revenue grew strongly on higher switch volumes and rising ASPs as AI racks push network bandwidth and interconnect needs. The target of roughly doubling 800G-and-above switch revenue this year is unchanged, and CPO optical switches are on plan for volume production and shipment in Q3 - CPO switches have already begun shipping, currently used mainly for scale-out links between AI racks and later extending as platform generations and system architecture upgrade. Foxconn is also building out optical modules, optoelectronic integration, advanced packaging, cables/connectors and high-speed transmission and power-management modules to lift in-house content; it sees optical communications and networking as the next major AI-infrastructure growth leg, with a market that could exceed US$100 billion, and its research institute announced an ultra-high-capacity silicon photonics technology for supercomputing transmission.
quarterly_data.figure: 800G+ switch revenue on track to double in 2026; CPO switch volume production and shipment from Q3

quarterly_data.signal: Inside its AI racks Foxconn integrates self-made high-value components - liquid cooling, power management, connectors, busbars, mechanical parts and high-speed transmission - with in-rack component self-sufficiency above half. Capex is being pre-committed to expand server, rack, liquid-cooling and test capacity globally, and high-power design, liquid-cooling systems, integration and test/validation are cited as the engineering barriers that keep raising the entry threshold for AI racks.

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor push advancing across capacity, key chips and design services: order visibility at Foxconn's 8-inch wafer fab in Japan now extends to Q4, and in-house silicon carbide, automotive MCU and AI power-IC programs are progressing on plan.
